min_age.rationale: 16 is the highest GDPR Art. 8 digital-consent age, so one rule covers every EU member state. It removes COPPA from scope and lowers the eating-disorder and compulsive-exercise risk for adolescents. Revisit 13+ for the US later, with counsel.

design_guardrails.rule: Never delete earned progress as a penalty. Stat decay is gradual detraining with a floor, and it pauses during declared rest, illness, injury, pregnancy, or travel.
design_guardrails.rationale: Punishment mechanics backfire (Habitica). Loss aversion recruits guilt-based motivation.

design_guardrails.rule: Do not highlight broken streaks. Use flexible weekly consistency goals, grace days, streak freezes, and unloseable best records.
design_guardrails.rationale: Highlighting a broken streak reduces subsequent engagement.

design_guardrails.rule: Use neutral, warm copy. No shame, guilt, or body-judgment language in the UI, pushes, or narrative.
design_guardrails.rationale: SDT: introjected (guilt and shame) regulation undermines sustained motivation.

design_guardrails.rule: Rest days are a rewarded quest type (recovery buffs and events).
design_guardrails.rationale: Overtraining results from excessive overload plus inadequate recovery.

design_guardrails.rule: Cap exertion-derived XP per day and per week. Weight XP toward consistency, not raw minutes or calories.
design_guardrails.rationale: Removes any incentive toward compulsive exercise or overtraining.

design_guardrails.rule: No rewards for multiple sessions per day or late-night workouts. Show a non-rewarding caution when training load spikes sharply week over week.
design_guardrails.rationale: Overtraining prevention. Thresholds need sports-science review.

design_guardrails.rule: No calories, weight, or BMI in the core loop or rewards. Any weight tracking is opt-in, private, unrewarded, and unranked.
design_guardrails.rationale: Calorie and fitness tracking is associated with eating-disorder symptoms. 73% of ED patients who used MyFitnessPal felt it contributed to their disorder.

design_guardrails.rule: Decouple avatar body shape from stats and fitness.
design_guardrails.rationale: Avoid body-image triggers. This is a design inference.

design_guardrails.rule: Returning players get a welcome-back quest sized to current ability and anchored to fresh-start landmarks (new week or month, birthday).
design_guardrails.rationale: Fresh start effect. Avoids the abstinence-violation spiral.

design_guardrails.rule: Sanctuary pause mode for illness, injury, travel, or caregiving suspends decay, quests, and reminders.
design_guardrails.rationale: Protects rest and avoids punishing legitimate lapses.

design_guardrails.rule: Pregnancy/postpartum mode: no intensity-based pressure, decay suspended, clinician-consult copy, and ACOG warning signs to stop exercising.
design_guardrails.rationale: ACOG CO 804 supports exercise in uncomplicated pregnancy, with warning signs.

design_guardrails.rule: Adaptive activity types (seated, wheelchair, low-impact, balance and strength). The user sets their own baseline. Progression is not step-count-only.
design_guardrails.rationale: WHO 2020: people with disabilities, chronic conditions, and older age should be active according to their ability.

design_guardrails.rule: Competitive leaderboards are opt-in. The default is cooperative party play and comparison with the user's own history.
design_guardrails.rationale: Supports relatedness and autonomy. Competition increased steps in STEP UP, but it is not suitable for everyone.

design_guardrails.rule: Notification quiet hours, no guilt-framed pushes, and a one-tap opt-out.
Offer a hide-numbers mode and links to eating-disorder and mental-health support resources.
design_guardrails.rationale: Quantification reduces enjoyment, and numeric focus can trigger ED symptoms.

design_guardrails.rule: Accessibility baseline: dynamic type, screen-reader labels, color-blind-safe cues, audio-optional quests.
design_guardrails.rationale: Inclusive design for disabilities and older adults.

design_guardrails.rule: No dark patterns in consent, subscription, or cancellation flows.
design_guardrails.rationale: Consistent with DSA Art. 25, the forthcoming Digital Fairness Act, and Apple 5.1.1(iv).

design_guardrails.rule: Use narrative and meaningful progression rather than points alone to sustain engagement past the novelty phase.
design_guardrails.rationale: The Pokémon GO step increase faded after about 6 weeks. The Zombies, Run! narrative supported long-term use.

compliance_requirements.requirement: Keep the intended purpose wellness-only (physical fitness, healthy activity) with no disease references, clinical thresholds, or abnormal labeling. Low-risk software only.
No medical intended purpose under MDR Art. 2(1) in labeling or marketing. Keep to lifestyle and well-being (Recital 19; MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1).
Explicit consent under Art. 9(2)(a) for health and fitness data, separate from the terms. Withdrawable, and logged.
DPIA (Art. 35), processor DPAs (Art. 28), an EU-US transfer mechanism or EU hosting, and an Art. 27 representative if there is no EU establishment.
Access, erasure, and portability: machine-readable export and full deletion.

Opt-in consent to collect consumer health data beyond what is necessary. A separate consent to share. Sale only with signed authorization (policy: never sell). A Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy. No geofencing within 2,000 ft of health facilities. Private right of action.
Separate consents for collecting and sharing consumer health data. Written authorization to sell. No geofence within 1,750 ft of health facilities.
Consumer-health-data controller duties apply regardless of thresholds: opt-in consent to sell, processor contracts, geofence limits. Health data is sensitive and needs consent.

Treat the app as a PHR vendor. Have a breach and unauthorized-disclosure response plan: notify individuals within 60 days, notify the FTC at the same time for 500+ affected, electronic and in-app notice. Penalties up to $53,088 per violation.

If thresholds are met: disclose sensitive PI, offer the right to limit, and complete a CPPA risk assessment for sensitive PI processing. Keep location coarser than an 1,850 ft radius to avoid the precise-geolocation category.
Map sensitive-data opt-in consent duties under other state privacy laws. Monitor the NY Health Information Privacy Act (vetoed Dec 2025, reintroduced 2026).
5.1.1(i) privacy policy in the app and metadata. 5.1.1(ii) consent, with an easy way to withdraw. 5.1.1(v) in-app account deletion.
5.1.2(vi)/5.1.3(i): no use of HealthKit or fitness data for ads, marketing, or data mining, and no sharing with third parties. Disclose the specific health data collected.
5.1.3(ii): do not store personal health information in iCloud (no CloudKit or iCloud KV sync of workout data). Do not write false data to HealthKit.
Submit as a legal entity (5.1.1(ix)). Complete the updated age-rating questionnaire and set a 16+ rating. 1.4.1: no unvalidated measurement-accuracy claims, and remind users to consult a doctor.

Complete the Health apps declaration and the Health Connect permissions declaration (use case: health-integrated game / fitness). Request only the minimum data types. No ads, sale, brokers, or insurance or credit use. Privacy policy in the Console and in the app. Encryption at rest and in transit.
Accurate Data safety form, including SDKs. In-app account deletion plus a web deletion URL in the Data safety form.
Display Strava-sourced data only to the owning user (no leaderboards or party feeds). No AI or ML model training on Strava data.
Neutral age gate at 16+. Block under-16 users and do not retain their data. Do not market to children.
If serving minors in the future, consume store age and consent signals and use them only for permitted purposes. Monitor litigation.
Monitor the Digital Fairness Act (addictive design and gamified rewards). Assess DSA online-platform status if public UGC is added.

In-app health and safety disclaimer at onboarding and in Settings: not medical advice, consult a physician before starting (especially if pregnant or living with a chronic condition), stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or chest pain.
Counsel review of all compliance positions, policies, and marketing copy before launch.

prohibited_claims: Diagnoses, detects, screens for, or monitors any disease or medical condition
Treats, cures, mitigates, or prevents any named disease (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, obesity, depression, anxiety)
Reduces risk of a specific disease (avoid even FDA category-2 claims unless counsel approves)
Rehabilitation, physical therapy, post-surgery, or post-injury recovery programs
Detects or diagnoses overtraining syndrome, injury, or any clinical state
Labels any user metric as abnormal, or references clinical thresholds or normal ranges
Clinical-grade or medical-device-equivalent accuracy for any measurement
Replaces or substitutes for a doctor, trainer's medical judgment, or medical device
Guaranteed or specific weight-loss results (e.g., 'lose 10 lbs in 30 days')
Mental-health treatment or therapy claims (e.g., 'treats depression')
FDA-approved, FDA-cleared, CE-marked, or clinically proven claims without substantiation
Safe for all pregnancies or all medical conditions
Any claim implying HealthKit, Health Connect, or Strava endorsement
